summary: Reproduced the reported Draft 2020-12 validation failure for a tool parameters schema containing required: null, then narrowly normalized that null sentinel to an omitted required keyword. The serving request validation regression and independent nested, valid-array, and malformed-non-null boundary cases pass. Upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35631 independently proposes a related broader change and was reviewed before implementation.

tests.what_was_measured: The prepared source left required: null unchanged and jsonschema raised the issue's exact None is not of type 'array' SchemaError. Raw output: reports/j-33266d7b6d72/raw/failing-before.txt
27 normalization tests and 3 malformed-required subtests passed, covering the regression, nested schemas, valid required arrays, and invalid non-null values that must remain rejected.
The actual OpenAIServingChat request validator accepts the reported schema shape and removes the null required sentinel before Draft 2020-12 validation.
The identical issue-shaped schema normalized to an object without required and passed Draft 2020-12 schema validation. Raw output: reports/j-33266d7b6d72/raw/passing-after.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned GPU was inventoried as one AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950 (reports/j-33266d7b6d72/raw/gpu-inventory.txt), but this defect occurs entirely in CPU-side HTTP request schema validation. No inference execution was used as evidence.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 weights and complete original request payload were not available, so no full-model or semantic tool-call reproduction is claimed.
The attached upstream server log confirms the Qwen3.8 server configuration and a 400 response but does not log the request body; the issue text supplies the exact validator error.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The open upstream PR #35631 also normalizes properties: null; that neighboring behavior was not included because issue #35242 specifically demonstrates required: null.
